answer: Each identity runs a lagoon depth station, locking an 80-credit bond. It posts canyon inflow/outflow readings and a crystal calibration record, key-bound to it, on the public lagoon board. Auditors recompute the balance: inflow minus outflow equals the lagoon change within 2 percent, else the bond burns. The k-th station pays 20+8(k-1) calibration credits, as sensors recalibrate per station; the 1,000th pays 8,012, so 1,000 fakes cost 4,096,000 total. A rented-calibration ring fails: one crystal record cannot fit two canyon flows. Honesty pays once; the bond returns after a clean epoch.
